title: Principles of Information Security
subtitle: Jeopardy Review — Practice Set B

jeopardyFormatExample.clueText: Encrypting a file at rest so that only the intended recipient can decode it upholds this CIA triad pillar.

categoryLegend: CIA & Foundations: Confidentiality (encryption at rest), Integrity (SHA-256 hash verification), attack surface, Availability (ransomware encryption), APT (multi-C2 persistence).  Threat Landscape: BEC/phishing, Trojan horse, virus, hacktivist, island-hopping.  Network Defense: packet-filtering (stateless) firewall, HIDS, DES (broken 56-bit), WAF, WireGuard.  OS & Hardening: need-to-know, AIDE/Tripwire (FIM), application allowlisting, TPM, SUID bit.  Security Mindset: something you have (FIDO2 key), DAC, separation of duties (code review), Eradication, defense in depth.

clues.clue: Encrypting a file at rest so that only the intended recipient can decode it upholds this CIA triad pillar.
clues.explain: Confidentiality ensures that data is readable only by authorized parties. Encryption at rest is a primary technical control that enforces it by rendering the data unintelligible without the correct key.

clues.clue: A software vendor publishes a SHA-256 hash alongside every installer download so users can confirm no one tampered with the file. This CIA triad component is being protected.
clues.explain: Integrity ensures data has not been altered by unauthorized parties. Publishing a cryptographic hash lets the recipient verify the file matches the original, detecting any tampering during transit.

clues.clue: A developer disables unused REST endpoints, removes debug logging from production, and closes three unneeded open ports. These actions all reduce this.
clues.explain: The attack surface is the sum of all points where an attacker could attempt to enter or extract data. Every removed endpoint, disabled service, or closed port shrinks it, reducing the number of exploitable footholds.

clues.clue: Ransomware encrypts every file on a hospital's file servers, preventing clinical staff from accessing patient records during surgery. This CIA triad component is most directly violated.
clues.explain: Availability ensures that systems and data are accessible when needed. Ransomware encryption renders files inaccessible, denying the service to authorized users -- an availability attack even though encryption is also involved.

clues.clue: A threat group infiltrates a defense contractor's network, establishes multiple backup command-and-control channels, and quietly exfiltrates documents for two years before detection.
clues.response: What is an APT (Advanced Persistent Threat)?
clues.explain: APTs maintain long-term, stealthy access through redundant footholds (multiple C2 channels, lateral movement) to conduct prolonged espionage. The hallmark is persistence and deliberate evasion over months or years.

clues.clue: An attacker sends an email appearing to come from the company CEO, asking an employee to wire funds immediately and keep it confidential. This social-engineering technique exploits authority and urgency.
clues.response: What is phishing (specifically Business Email Compromise or BEC)?
clues.explain: Business Email Compromise is a phishing variant where attackers impersonate executives to pressure employees into wire transfers or credential disclosure. It exploits authority and manufactured urgency rather than technical exploits.

clues.clue: Malware that poses as a legitimate utility -- such as a free video converter -- but secretly opens a backdoor once installed.
clues.explain: A Trojan disguises itself as benign or useful software to trick users into running it, then executes a hidden malicious payload such as a backdoor, keylogger, or RAT -- unlike a virus or worm, it does not self-replicate.

clues.clue: This class of malware attaches a copy of itself to legitimate executable files and spreads when those infected files are shared or executed by other users.
clues.explain: A virus injects its code into a host executable and spreads when that host file is copied or executed. Unlike a worm it requires a carrier file and typically user action to propagate.

clues.clue: This category of threat actor is typically driven by political or ideological goals, defacing websites or leaking data to draw attention to a cause rather than for financial gain.
clues.explain: Hacktivists use hacking as a form of protest or activism, motivated by ideology rather than money. Common tactics include website defacement, DDoS attacks, and data dumps intended to embarrass a target or publicize a cause.

clues.clue: An attacker compromises a law firm's email server and uses it to send a malicious invoice to every one of that firm's corporate clients, exploiting the established trust relationship.
clues.explain: Island-hopping (supply-chain phishing) compromises a trusted third party and uses that trusted identity or channel to reach a high-value secondary target. The trust relationship -- here the law firm -- is the weapon, making detection far harder than generic phishing.

clues.clue: The earliest and simplest type of firewall, which filters traffic solely by inspecting individual packet headers (source/destination IP, port, protocol) without any connection state memory.
clues.explain: A packet-filtering firewall evaluates each packet in isolation against a rule set of IP addresses, ports, and protocols. Because it stores no connection state, it is fast but cannot detect attacks that span multiple packets.

clues.clue: An IDS sensor placed directly on a host OS, monitoring local system calls, log files, and filesystem changes rather than network traffic.
clues.response: What is a HIDS (Host-based Intrusion Detection System)?
clues.explain: A HIDS runs on the individual host and monitors internal events -- system calls, log entries, file changes -- to detect compromise. It sees encrypted traffic in plaintext at the host level, unlike a network-based IDS which only sees the wire.

clues.clue: The older symmetric cipher that uses 56-bit keys and is now considered broken because those keys can be brute-forced in under 24 hours with modern hardware.
clues.explain: DES was adopted as the US federal standard in 1977 but its 56-bit key space is exhaustively searchable with modern hardware. It was replaced by Triple-DES and then AES; NIST officially withdrew it in 2005.

clues.clue: A security device deployed inline in front of a web application that can inspect HTTP/HTTPS traffic and block requests matching signatures for SQL injection and cross-site scripting.
clues.response: What is a WAF (Web Application Firewall)?
clues.explain: A WAF sits inline between clients and a web server, inspecting HTTP/HTTPS requests against rule sets for OWASP Top 10 attacks like SQLi and XSS. Unlike a network firewall it operates at Layer 7 and understands application-layer context.

clues.clue: This modern, open-source VPN protocol uses the Noise Protocol Framework and ChaCha20-Poly1305 encryption; it has a codebase under 5,000 lines, making it far easier to audit than its predecessors.
clues.explain: WireGuard is a modern VPN protocol designed for simplicity and speed. Its minimal codebase (~4,000 lines vs tens of thousands for OpenVPN/IPSec) reduces audit surface, and its use of modern cryptographic primitives (ChaCha20-Poly1305, Curve25519) delivers strong performance.

clues.clue: A closely related security principle to least privilege: a user is granted access to only the specific data relevant to their current task, not an entire database or file share.
clues.explain: Need-to-know restricts access to information to only what is required for a specific role or task, even among users who hold a sufficient clearance level. It complements least privilege by limiting data exposure beyond what permissions alone define.

clues.clue: On Linux, this command-line tool from the AIDE or Tripwire family creates a cryptographic baseline of system files and alerts when any file's hash deviates from that baseline.
clues.response: What is a file integrity monitor (FIM) such as AIDE or Tripwire?
clues.explain: File integrity monitors (AIDE, Tripwire) hash critical system binaries and configurations at a known-good baseline, then periodically re-hash and alert on any mismatch -- detecting rootkits, unauthorized changes, or configuration drift.

clues.clue: A Windows security control that maintains a list of explicitly approved applications and blocks any executable not on that list from running, preventing unknown malware from executing.
clues.explain: Application allowlisting (formerly whitelisting) permits only explicitly approved executables to run. It inverts the traditional blocklist approach and is one of the most effective attack-surface reduction controls because unknown malware is blocked by default.

clues.clue: This hardware security component, specified in ISO/IEC 11889, stores cryptographic keys, performs remote attestation, and provides a hardware root of trust that Secure Boot and BitLocker rely on.
clues.response: What is a TPM (Trusted Platform Module)?
clues.explain: A TPM is a dedicated hardware chip that securely generates and stores cryptographic keys and measurements of the boot environment. Secure Boot checks signatures; the TPM provides the hardware root of trust and enables attestation -- proving to a remote verifier that the system booted in an expected state.

clues.clue: On Linux, this special permission bit on an executable causes it to run with the file OWNER's privileges rather than the calling user's, enabling tools like passwd to write to /etc/shadow.
clues.response: What is the SUID bit (Set User ID, shown as 's' in the owner execute position)?
clues.explain: The SUID bit causes an executable to run as the file's owner (often root) instead of the invoking user. It allows privileged programs like passwd to modify /etc/shadow, but misconfigured SUID binaries are a classic privilege-escalation vector.

clues.clue: A hardware FIDO2 security key that a user physically plugs into a USB port to complete authentication falls into this MFA factor category.
clues.response: What is something you have (a possession factor)?
clues.explain: MFA factor categories are something you know (password/PIN), something you have (token, smart card, FIDO2 key), and something you are (biometric). A hardware security key is a possession factor; because it must be physically present, it resists remote phishing of one-time codes.

clues.clue: The access control model where the resource owner decides who may access their files -- such as a file owner setting read/write permissions for other users in a standard Linux or Windows file system.
clues.explain: In DAC the resource owner has discretion to grant or revoke access to their objects. Standard POSIX file permissions and Windows NTFS ACLs implement DAC; its weakness is that owners can inadvertently share data too broadly.

clues.clue: A software development organization requires that the engineer who writes a code change CANNOT also be the person who approves and merges it into production. This is an application of which control?
clues.explain: Separation of duties prevents the same individual from performing all steps of a sensitive process end-to-end. In software delivery, requiring a separate reviewer and approver for code merges prevents a single insider from introducing and concealing malicious changes.

clues.clue: In the NIST SP 800-61 incident response lifecycle, the phase immediately following containment, during which malware is removed, compromised accounts are reset, and vulnerable systems are patched.
clues.explain: The NIST SP 800-61 phases are Preparation, Detection and Analysis, Containment, Eradication, Recovery, and Post-Incident Activity. Eradication follows containment and removes all traces of the threat -- malware, backdoors, rogue accounts -- before systems are returned to service.

clues.clue: The reason security architects insist on BOTH network-layer firewall rules AND host-based firewall rules for the same server, even though it seems redundant, is rooted in this strategy.
clues.explain: Defense in depth deliberately uses overlapping, independent controls at multiple layers (network, host, application, data) so that bypassing one does not expose the asset. The apparent redundancy is intentional: if a misconfigured network rule lets a packet through, the host firewall remains as the next barrier.
